title: Runway vs Kling: shared models, editing and workflow costs
summary: Compare Runway with Kling’s own app: shared Kling models, Gen-4.5, Edit Studio, reference controls and project costs. Choose the route that fits your footage.
body_markdown:
Choose Runway when your project needs its generation and editing tools together. Choose Kling’s own app when its direct reference and keyframe workflows fit the work. Runway also offers Kling models, so this is a platform decision, not simply Gen-4.5 versus Kling. Compare the exact model, operation, inputs and account quote before judging the result or buying more capacity.


Magic Hour publishes this documentation-based comparison. Official product routes and terms were checked November 3, 2026. We did not run a retained Runway-versus-Kling output-quality test.


## The decision at a glance


Decision


Runway


Kling


Primary decision


A workspace combining its own models, hosted models and editing tools.


The provider’s own app and direct Kling creation modes.


Creating new shots


Choose the specific model; Gen-4.5 and hosted Kling are different options.


Choose the Kling model and supported direct-app mode.


Editing existing footage


Evaluate Edit Studio’s edited-keyframe preview and video transformation.


Evaluate the selected direct editing/reference workflow.


Required inputs and output


Hosted-model controls can differ from the direct app.


Check mode-specific references and actual account settings.


Reason to choose it


Its combined workflow reduces the work around each approved clip.


Its direct controls finish the project without a wider workspace.


## Runway and Kling are not mutually exclusive models


Runway’s consumer product page explicitly offers Kling 4.0 alongside its own models and other providers. A Runway subscription can therefore be a route to Kling, rather than a decision to avoid it. The useful question is which workspace and controls help you finish the project.


Separate two comparisons. To compare models, use the same supported inputs and label the selected versions. To compare platforms, include preparation, edits, exports and billing. A better result from Kling inside Runway would not prove that Runway’s own model beat Kling.


Sources:[Kling 4.0 in Runway’s creative workspace](https://runway.com/product/models/kling-4.0)


## Choose Runway for generation plus directed edits


Runway is worth shortlisting when a project needs new shots and changes to footage you already have. Gen-4.5 supports text-to-video and image-to-video; the current guide lists two-to-ten-second generation and 720p output. Editing an existing clip is a different operation.


Edit Studio uses Aleph 2.0. You can select a source keyframe, describe the change and review an edited image before generating the video transformation. For a product shot needing a different background, that preview step gives you a concrete appearance decision before processing the moving sequence. It does not guarantee that the final video preserves every detail.


Check the upload rules first. The current Edit Studio guide documents limits for clip length, resolution, frame rate and cuts, and identifies Single edit as available while other modes are coming soon. Do not treat every announced editing mode as a present tool.


Sources:[Creating with Gen-4.5](https://help.runwayml.com/hc/en-us/articles/46974685288467-Creating-with-Gen-4-5) ·[Edit Studio inputs and keyframe-led editing](https://help.runwayml.com/hc/en-us/articles/51683104370451-Creating-with-Edit-Studio)


## Choose Kling directly for its creation modes


Start with Kling’s own app when you mainly use its model family and its direct controls suit your assets. The official guide distinguishes Omni Reference from Keyframes. One organizes material that guides the scene; the other defines visual moments along the timeline. Choose the mode before preparing a large reference pack.


For example, a sequence guided by separate character and action references differs from a shot with predetermined opening and closing compositions. Write down what each asset contributes and inspect the resulting sequence. These are illustrative planning choices, not evidence that direct access produces better-looking video than the same model elsewhere.


Sources:[Kling 4.0 modes and input requirements](https://kling.ai/quickstart/kling-4-model-user-guide)


## Check the route for audio and export requirements


Runway’s Kling 4.0 page lists 720p and 1080p, generated sound and image/video references. It explicitly says audio files cannot be attached as references there. If a supplied voice reference is essential, check Kling’s direct Omni workflow and its account controls instead of assuming the hosted route accepts the same inputs.


The Runway page marks native Kling 4.0 4K as not yet available. Kling’s broader guide also contains rollout qualifications, including HDR and longer extension described as coming soon. Keep the exact route in your delivery brief; neither a model name nor a broad specification table proves your account can produce the required file today.


Sources:[Runway’s Kling 4.0 reference and export FAQ](https://runway.com/product/models/kling-4.0) ·[Kling’s direct guide and rollout qualifications](https://kling.ai/quickstart/kling-4-model-user-guide)


## Compare one small project without inventing a price winner


Suppose you need six approved five-second shots and budget two candidates per shot. That is twelve attempts and sixty generated seconds for thirty seconds of final footage. This is a hypothetical worksheet, not an observed acceptance rate.


Record the quote for each viable route, including model, operation, resolution and audio. Add paid edits, rejected attempts, required finishing and the minimum purchase. Divide total project spending by six approved shots. Keep upfront cash separate from the value of the credits actually consumed.


Use a published rate only for the operation it describes. A Gen-4.5 generation charge cannot price an Aleph edit or a Kling request. Vendor credits also have different purchase prices. For detailed plan context, use the Runway pricing guide and Kling pricing guide, then recheck the quote in the actual account.


Sources:[Runway pricing guide](https://magichour.ai/blog/runway-ml-pricing) ·[Kling pricing guide](https://magichour.ai/blog/kling-ai-pricing) ·[Current Gen-4.5 specification](https://help.runwayml.com/hc/en-us/articles/46974685288467-Creating-with-Gen-4-5)


## Keep commercial rights separate from the export


Runway’s usage-rights guidance permits commercial use of creations, subject to its terms. Kling’s general terms and paid-service terms must be read together: membership provides commercial-output benefits, while the general terms restrict unpermitted commercial use. Check the agreement for the platform actually generating your file.


A usable download is another question. Confirm watermark, resolution and the intended distribution, and obtain rights to reference footage, voices and likenesses. Permission from the tool does not supply permission from the people or asset owners represented in the video.


Sources:[Runway usage rights](https://help.runwayml.com/hc/en-us/articles/18927776141715-Usage-rights) ·[Kling general terms](https://kling.ai/docs/user-policy) ·[Kling paid-service benefits](https://kling.ai/docs/payment-policy)


## When staying is the better choice


Stay with your existing platform when it already produces accepted work under suitable terms and a manageable total cost. Move one representative project before moving a production calendar. Preserve inputs, prompts, settings and accepted files so the comparison does not become a test of different source material.


Choose Runway when its combined generation and editing workflow removes real work. Choose Kling directly when its creation modes and purchase terms meet the project more simply. For another platform comparison, read Runway vs Higgsfield or Higgsfield vs Kling. Neither a larger model list nor direct access establishes a universal quality winner.


Sources:[Runway vs Higgsfield](https://magichour.ai/blog/runway-vs-higgsfield) ·[Higgsfield vs Kling](https://magichour.ai/blog/higgsfield-vs-kling)
